chunks.label: Happiness and thanks
chunks.rationale: Lets you say you're happy, grateful, smiling or still hopeful.
chunks.interference: Shiawase is deep happiness; for 'glad about this one thing' learners should still reach for ureshii.

chunks.label: Relief and worry
chunks.rationale: Lets you say a worry has lifted or is still there, and whether you're satisfied.
chunks.interference: Two pairs that sound alike: anshin / fuan and manzoku / fuman.

chunks.label: Likes and love
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk about your type, your love life, jealousy and what bores you.
chunks.interference: Ren'ai is romance as a topic, not loving one person (suki).

chunks.label: When I was little
chunks.rationale: Lets you start a story about your childhood or the past.
chunks.interference: Touji (at the time) and toujitsu (on the day) sound alike.

chunks.label: Memories and stories
chunks.rationale: Lets you tell a memory: what happened one day and what you remember.
chunks.interference: Omoide is a fond memory; kioku is what your brain stored.

chunks.label: Moments and nowadays
chunks.rationale: Lets you place things in time: for a second, right about now, earlier, these days.

chunks.label: Before, during, last time
chunks.rationale: Lets you place things around an event: on the way, last time, right before, on the day.
chunks.interference: Toujitsu (on the day) vs touji (at the time).

chunks.label: The future and chances
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk about what's ahead and the chances you get.
chunks.interference: Kikai (an opportunity) vs kanousei (a likelihood); shourai vs mirai for 'future'.

chunks.label: Relationships and boundaries
chunks.rationale: Lets you ask how people are connected and say what's your own business.
chunks.interference: Jiyuu means free to choose, not free of charge.

chunks.label: Reasons and facts
chunks.rationale: Lets you give the why, the facts, the backstory and who's to blame.
chunks.interference: Jijitsu (fact) vs jitsu wa (actually) vs jijou (circumstances).

chunks.label: Effort and attitude
chunks.rationale: Lets you say someone means it, tries hard, is brave, proud or rude.

chunks.label: Talent and skill
chunks.rationale: Lets you praise or judge what someone can do.
chunks.interference: All three translate as 'ability': sainou is inborn, jitsuryoku is proven, nouryoku is general.

chunks.label: Shock and hard times
chunks.rationale: Lets you say something hurt, was awful, or was a hard thing to go through.
chunks.interference: Shokku means hurt and let down, not surprised (bikkuri).

chunks.label: Dreams and reality
chunks.rationale: Lets you set ideals and miracles against harsh reality.

chunks.label: Special occasions
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk about firsts, ceremonies and marking a day.
chunks.interference: Hatsu (first ever) vs hajimete (for the first time).

chunks.label: Situations and ways
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk about what's going on, how things stand, and what to do if.

chunks.label: Sensing and feeling
chunks.rationale: Lets you say something feels off, you've got a hunch, or you can't feel your hands.
chunks.interference: Kankaku (sensation) vs kanjou (emotion), both 'feeling' in English.
